name: Film / TV Production Crew
description: Project-based organizational structure for film and television production. Built around a clear creative and business command chain operating for the duration of production, then disbanding. Distinguishes between above-the-line (directors, producers, principal talent) and below-the-line (crew, technicians, crafts) personnel.

org_structure.overview: Film and TV productions are temporary, project-based organizations assembled for a specific production and dissolved upon completion. The structure follows a clear hierarchical command chain with two parallel leadership tracks: creative (Director) and business (Producer). Department heads manage specialized crews in their craft areas. Above-the-line roles include the director, producers, and principal cast; below-the-line encompasses all technical and craft crew. Reporting lines are direct during production but the entire organization is transient, with crew moving between projects.

departments.name: Executive / Above-the-Line
departments.description: Senior creative and business leadership responsible for the overall production vision, financing, and delivery. Includes the Director (creative authority), Producers (business and logistics authority), Writer(s), and Principal Cast.

roles.title: Director
roles.description: Creative visionary responsible for storytelling, performances, visual style, and overall artistic direction of the production.

roles.title: Producer
roles.description: Oversees all business aspects: financing, scheduling, hiring key personnel, and ensuring the production delivers on time and on budget.

roles.title: Executive Producer
roles.description: Senior financial or creative stakeholder; may secure funding, attach talent, or provide high-level oversight without day-to-day involvement.

roles.title: Line Producer
roles.description: Manages the day-to-day physical production budget, logistics, and crew hiring; the bridge between creative ambitions and financial reality.

roles.title: Screenwriter
roles.description: Writes or adapts the screenplay; may be attached during pre-production and rewrites during production.

roles.title: Unit Production Manager
roles.description: Oversees scheduling, location logistics, crew travel, and daily production operations.

departments.name: Camera & Electrical
departments.description: Responsible for all visual capture, lighting, and on-set electrical work. Led by the Director of Photography (DP) who translates the director's vision into camera and lighting choices.

roles.title: Director of Photography (DP/Cinematographer)
roles.description: Designs the visual look of the film: lighting, camera placement, lens choice, color palette. Supervises the entire camera and lighting crew.

roles.title: Camera Operator
roles.description: Physically operates the camera during takes, following blocking and framing instructions from the DP and director.

roles.title: 1st Assistant Camera (1st AC)
roles.description: Responsible for camera assembly, lens changes, pulling focus during takes, and managing camera prep and wrap.

roles.title: 2nd Assistant Camera (2nd AC)
roles.description: Loads magazines, operates clapperboard/slate, manages camera reports, and assists with media management.

roles.title: Gaffer
roles.description: Head of electrical department; designs and executes lighting plans, manages generators, ballasts, and lighting crew.

roles.title: Best Boy Electric
roles.description: Second-in-command of electrical; manages equipment rental, crew scheduling, and acts as gaffer's lead assistant.

roles.title: Lighting Technician / Electrician
roles.description: Sets up, operates, and strikes lighting equipment; runs cable and maintains electrical safety on set.

roles.title: Key Grip
roles.description: Leads grip department: manages non-electrical lighting support (diffusers, flags, stands), camera rigging (dolly, crane, stabilizers), and set shading.

roles.title: Best Boy Grip
roles.description: Assistant to Key Grip; manages grip equipment inventory, crew assignments, and safety inspections.

roles.title: Grip
roles.description: Builds and operates camera support equipment: dollies, cranes, tracks, tripods, and lighting modification rigs.

departments.name: Art Department
departments.description: Designs and builds the physical environment of the film including sets, props, and visual aesthetic. Translates the director's vision into tangible spaces and objects.

roles.title: Production Designer
roles.description: Creates the overall visual environment: set design, color palette, texture, and period accuracy. Supervises art, set decoration, and construction teams.

roles.title: Art Director
roles.description: Manages the art department budget, schedules, and construction; translates designer concepts into buildable plans and supervises drafting and model-making.

roles.title: Set Decorator
roles.description: Selects and arranges all furnishings, drapery, wallpaper, and decorative items that dress the set according to the period and story requirements.

roles.title: Props Master
roles.description: Acquires, builds, tracks, and maintains all hand props—objects actors handle during the production.

roles.title: Set Dresser
roles.description: Places and arranges set decoration elements on set; handles dressing and striking sets between scenes.

roles.title: Leadman
roles.description: Supervises the set dressing crew on the floor; coordinates with construction and other departments on set dressing schedules.

roles.title: Storyboard Artist
roles.description: Creates visual storyboards of key scenes illustrating camera angles, blocking, and composition for pre-visualization.

roles.title: Construction Coordinator
roles.description: Oversees set construction: manages carpentry crews, materials purchasing, and ensures sets are built to spec and on schedule.

roles.title: Greensperson
roles.description: Responsible for all live plant and floral elements on set; sources, installs, and maintains greenery.

departments.name: Sound Department
departments.description: Captures all location audio including dialogue, ambient sound, and effects. Ensures clean, usable audio for post-production.

roles.title: Production Sound Mixer
roles.description: Records all on-set audio; responsible for microphone selection, mixing multiple audio sources, and delivering clean production sound.

roles.title: Boom Operator
roles.description: Positions and operates the boom microphone to capture dialogue; monitors for unwanted noise and maintains microphone placement during takes.

roles.title: Sound Utility
roles.description: Assists with wireless microphone setup (lavaliers), cable management, labeling, and sound department logistics.

departments.name: Hair, Makeup & Wardrobe
departments.description: Responsible for actor appearance continuity including hairstyling, makeup application, special effects makeup, and costume management throughout the production.

roles.title: Makeup Department Head
roles.description: Designs the makeup looks for all characters; manages makeup crew, product budgets, and ensures continuity of makeup across scenes.

roles.title: Key Makeup Artist
roles.description: Applies makeup to principal cast; maintains character looks and ensures screen-ready appearance for every take.

roles.title: Special Effects Makeup Artist
roles.description: Creates prosthetic appliances, wounds, aging effects, and creature makeup requiring advanced sculpting and application techniques.

roles.title: Hair Department Head
roles.description: Designs and manages all hairstyling for the production; oversees wig creation, period styling, and hair continuity.

roles.title: Key Hairstylist
roles.description: Styles and maintains principal cast hair; manages daily hair prep, wig application, and quick changes.

roles.title: Costume Designer
roles.description: Researches, designs, and oversees creation of all costumes; establishes character wardrobe reflecting story, period, and personality.

roles.title: Wardrobe Supervisor
roles.description: Manages costume inventory, fittings, alterations, laundry, and continuity tracking for all wardrobe items across the shoot.

roles.title: Set Costumer
roles.description: Dresses actors on set, manages quick changes, maintains costume condition, and assists with continuity photos.

departments.name: Stunts & Stunts Safety
departments.description: Plans, choreographs, and executes all action sequences and stunts safely. Manages risk assessment, rigging, and performer safety.

roles.title: Stunt Coordinator
roles.description: Designs and supervises all stunt sequences; hires stunt performers, conducts safety briefings, and approves rigging and protection measures.

roles.title: Stunt Performer / Double
roles.description: Performs stunts including fights, falls, driving, fire, and high-risk action; may double for principal cast in dangerous scenes.

roles.title: Stunt Rigging Technician
roles.description: Installs and tests stunt rigging equipment: wires, harnesses, air rams, breakaway props, and safety systems.

departments.name: Production Office & Logistics
departments.description: Handles the administrative, logistical, and operational backbone of the production including scheduling, locations, talent, and craft services.

roles.title: Production Coordinator
roles.description: Central communications hub; manages call sheets, production reports, crew travel, and office coordination.

roles.title: Assistant Director (1st AD)
roles.description: Runs the set: creates the shooting schedule, manages crew calls, enforces safety, and ensures the day's work is completed on time.

roles.title: 2nd Assistant Director (2nd AD)
roles.description: Creates call sheets and daily production reports; wrangles background actors and manages set timing.

roles.title: 3rd Assistant Director (3rd AD)
roles.description: Assists with background actor management, set locking, and runner duties as directed by senior AD staff.

roles.title: Location Manager
roles.description: Secures filming locations, negotiates permits and fees, manages location logistics, and serves as liaison with local authorities and communities.

roles.title: Location Assistant
roles.description: Supports location scouting, manages parking and base camp, directs crew and vehicles to locations, and handles crowd control.

roles.title: Craft Service / Caterer
roles.description: Provides meals, snacks, and beverages for cast and crew throughout production days; manages dietary restrictions and set hospitality.

roles.title: Casting Director
roles.description: Auditions and selects actors for all roles; manages casting sessions, negotiates talent deals, and coordinates with agents.

roles.title: Script Supervisor
roles.description: Maintains script continuity across takes; tracks dialogue changes, screen direction, and ensures editorial consistency.

roles.title: Transportation Coordinator
roles.description: Manages all production vehicles including picture cars, crew vans, honeywagons, and equipment trucks; oversees drivers and fueling.

departments.name: Post-Production
departments.description: Handles all work after principal photography: editing, visual effects, sound design, color grading, music composition, and final mastering.

roles.title: Editor
roles.description: Assembles footage into the final narrative; works with the director on pacing, performance selection, and structural edits.

roles.title: Assistant Editor
roles.description: Ingests and syncs footage, organizes media, manages project files, preps sequences, and outputs review copies.

roles.title: Visual Effects Supervisor
roles.description: Oversees all visual effects work: green screen, CGI, compositing; manages VFX vendors, bids, and creative direction of digital effects.

roles.title: Composer
roles.description: Creates original musical score for the film; works to picture to underscore emotional beats and narrative arcs.

roles.title: Sound Designer / Re-recording Mixer
roles.description: Creates the final audio landscape: dialogue clean-up, ADR, Foley, sound effects, and final mix balancing dialogue, music, and effects.

roles.title: Colorist
roles.description: Performs color grading and correction; establishes the final color palette and visual tone of each scene in post-production.

key_relationships: Director and Director of Photography collaborate closely on visual storytelling and camera language throughout pre-production and production.
Producer and Line Producer maintain constant communication on budget status, schedule changes, and resource allocation.
Director and Editor work intensively during post-production to shape the final narrative from raw footage.
1st Assistant Director serves as the on-set operational leader, coordinating between all departments to keep the shooting schedule on track.
Production Designer and Costume Designer coordinate on color palettes and visual world-building to maintain cohesive aesthetic.
Gaffer and Key Grip work in tandem under the DP to achieve lighting setups, with electrical and grip equipment operating as complementary systems.
Stunt Coordinator coordinates with Director, 1st AD, and Safety Officer to ensure all action sequences are properly risk-assessed and rehearsed.
Makeup, Hair, and Wardrobe departments operate adjacent to each other, often sharing workspace and coordinating actor prep timelines.
Unit Production Manager coordinates with all department heads to align crew schedules, equipment needs, and location logistics.
Production Sound Mixer coordinates with the Director and 1st AD to manage quiet on set and ensure optimal audio capture conditions.
